methods.label: Eliminate both variables
methods.explanation:
The variable terms in the second equation are \(-2\) times those in the first, so elimination will test whether their constants are compatible. Multiplying the first equation by \(2\) gives
\[
4x-6y=16.
\]
Adding this to \(6y-4x=9\) yields
\[
0=25.
\]
Any common solution would have to satisfy this equality, which is impossible. Therefore there is no solution, choice D.
methods.levelReason: Multiplying and adding equations reveals an inconsistency using elementary equality properties.
